name: esp2023_lock_gates
story: The paddles lift to empty the lock through the gates, then the two leaves open into their recesses and shut again, each driven by its own electric actuator in its inspection chamber, and the paddles drop. Real time is about 60 s for each leaf; this runs 10 times faster.

steps.title: Open the Dynamic Simulation environment
steps.command: Environments tab > Begin panel > Dynamic Simulation
actions: Open esp2023_lock_gates.iam in Inventor.
Click the Environments tab, then Dynamic Simulation.
steps.note: Dynamic Simulation works out how an assembly moves, and the forces and speeds as it moves.

steps.title: Turn constraints into joints
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Settings
actions: Click Simulation Settings and tick Automatically convert constraints to standard joints. Click OK.
Open Standard Joints in the browser to see the joints Inventor made from your assembly constraints.
steps.note: Parts held together with no movement between them become one rigid group, listed under Welded group.

steps.title: Check the hinge joints
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Joint panel > Insert Joint
actions: In Standard Joints find the Revolution joint for each leaf: the pintle bush on the bottom pintle, and the heel post journal in the collar bush.
If a leaf has two joints (one at the top and one at the bottom) Inventor shows the second as redundant. Keep one Revolution joint per leaf, on the pivot axis, and delete the other.
Every part of the leaf sub-assembly (frame, fenders, seals, walkway, paddle guides) should be one Welded group.
steps.note: A revolution joint lets a part turn about one axis and nothing else: one degree of freedom.

steps.title: Join the actuators
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Joint panel > Insert Joint
actions: Each actuator needs three joints. Insert Joint, Revolution: the actuator body rear eye on the pivot pin.
Insert Joint, Cylindrical: the rod inside the body bore, so the rod can slide out.
Insert Joint, Revolution: the rod end eye on the front pivot pin in the leaf bracket.
steps.note: The rod end has a spherical bearing, so the actuator can follow the leaf as it swings.

steps.title: Join the paddles
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Joint panel > Insert Joint
actions: Insert Joint, Prismatic: the paddle door sliding up the paddle guides. The paddle rod is welded to the door.
Right click the joint > Properties > dof 1 (T) > Edit imposed motion: 0 at 0.5 s, 500 mm at 2 s, hold, back to 0 at 19.5 s.
steps.note: The paddles let the lock empty through the gates first: the gates can only open when the water is level on both sides.

steps.title: Drive the leaves
steps.command: Right click a leaf Revolution joint > Properties > dof 1 (R) > Edit imposed motion
actions: Tick Enable imposed motion. Drive: Position.
Right leaf, in the Input Grapher: 0 degrees at 3 s, -71.6 degrees (fully open) at 9 s, hold to 11 s, back to 0 at 17 s.
Left leaf: the same, but +71.6 degrees, starting half a second later, so you can see the leaves work independently.
Click OK twice.
steps.note: The real gates take about 60 s to open. This simulation runs 10 times faster. Each leaf turns 71.6 degrees, from the mitre (1 in 3) into its recess in the lock wall.

steps.title: Check the actuator stroke
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Joint panel > Insert Joint
actions: Right click the actuator Cylindrical joint > Properties and look at dof 2 (T): Inventor works out how far the rod slides as the leaf turns.
Pin to pin length: 3301 mm with the gate shut and 2045 mm with it open, a stroke of 1256 mm.
Check the rod never pulls out of the body: at full length 199 mm of the rod is still inside.
steps.note: Choose an actuator with at least this stroke. A 1300 mm stroke electric actuator gives some spare.

steps.title: Run the simulation
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Player
actions: In the Simulation Player set Final Time to 20 s and Images to 1000.
Click Run. The assembly moves and the timeline fills in.
Use the slider to scrub back and forth.
steps.note: Press Play below to run the same motion here.

steps.title: Plot the results
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Results panel > Output Grapher
actions: Open the Output Grapher.
Under Standard Joints, tick the angle of each leaf Revolution joint, the position of the actuator Cylindrical joint and the paddle Prismatic joint.
The graph shows each value against time. Click on the graph to move the simulation to that moment.

steps.title: Record a video
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Player
actions: In the Simulation Player click Record (the red dot) and choose a file name and format.
Click Run again. Inventor saves a video of the motion for your portfolio.
steps.note: You can also export a moment to Stress Analysis (Export to FEA) to check a part at its highest load.
